source: NAR 2026 Technology Report; California DRE; Real Estate News

headline: Your AI, your
*responsibility*
slides.fig_caption: of Realtors use AI every day, per NAR's 2026 tech report
slides.sub: Adoption is climbing fast, and regulators are spelling out who answers when AI gets it wrong.

slides.title: Nearly half, *every week*
slides.note: Only *12%* have no plans to use AI. In 2025, 32% hadn't tried it.

slides.kicker: Top uses among agents who use AI
slides.title: What agents hand to *AI*
slides.note: The top AI task is the copy buyers see first: *the listing*.

slides.title: The tool isn't *the excuse*
points: *California's DRE:* licensees and brokers, not software vendors, own AI mistakes.
*No AI defense:* using AI doesn't excuse a misleading ad or an inaccurate claim.
*Altered photos:* since Jan. 1, 2026, California requires disclosing AI-changed listing images and offering the originals.
*NAR's AI policy kit:* agents and staff are fully accountable for the AI content they use.

slides.title: Check it *before you send it*
slides.body: Use AI for first drafts, not final answers. Verify comps, property facts and photos against reliable sources, and only share what you can explain to a client yourself.
